added.name: Altair Health
added.long_description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean from the first patient, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on.

added.name: Praxis
added.long_description:
At Praxis, we’ve built AI agents that run law firm operations, from first inquiry to paid invoice. Agents do the admin end to end, and the lawyer supervises and approves every step. Firms reply in minutes, onboard clients in days instead of weeks, and spend their time practicing law.

Lawyers spend 62% of their day on admin nobody pays for: intake, conflict checks, chasing documents, engagement letters, follow-ups, billing. Every hour on admin is an hour a client waits, and clients go to the firm that answers first. One law firm owner shared: “Every month we lose 3-5 clients, $10k each, because we’re 3 paralegals to handle the process, it’s too slow.”

We’re live with law firms across the US.
added.one_liner: AI agents that run law firm operations.

added.name: Graphide
added.long_description: Graphide (YC F26) is a code editor that maps your codebase into a graph so you can see what your agents are building. Agents now write code faster than anyone can read it, and a line by line diff doesn't show what actually changed in the system. Graphide keeps a live graph of the modules, classes, functions, etc. how they connect, and what each agent is touching as it works. Graphide then checks their changes against your architecture, making sure your agents are implementing what you had in mind.
added.one_liner: A graph based IDE for when agents program faster than you can read

long_description.before:
OctaPulse uses AI vision to automate hatchery QA for fish farms, starting with broodstock phenotyping and juvenile deformity inspection. We cut inspection time from about 5 minutes to under 30 seconds per fish, with more than 90 percent accuracy, so farms advance only high quality fish and waste less feed and labor. Our goal is to bring automation across the entire fish production lifecycle for the $300B aquaculture industry.

Aquaculture is the fastest growing food sector, and has already surpassed commercial fishing for production of seafood. Yet two of the most critical QA and QC steps in fish production are still done by hand: phenotyping and deformity inspection. These processes are slow, error prone, and despised by technicians but vital for the success of the farm, so much so that farms spend >$200K a year on trained technicians and geneticists to operate. We’ve built an AI vision platform for vertically integrated finfish farms that drops into existing workflows starting in the hatchery, uses off the shelf cameras, standardizes these QA steps, and creates a proprietary multi species dataset that becomes the brain for future autonomous aquafarms. Phenotyping is the start, but the platform is designed to be a drop in solution that can easily expand into feeding, health monitoring, and processing so we can solve production problems across the lifecycle.

 We signed a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, are deploying into 2 more farms early 2026, and trained models above 90 percent accuracy while cutting inspection time from 5 minutes to under 30 seconds. Each deployment adds labeled images to our dataset and improves cross species generalization.
long_description.after:
OctaPulse is building the robotics layer for seafood production. Aquaculture is the fastest-growing food sector and already produces more seafood than commercial fishing, yet the people who breed and process fish still make thousands of decisions a day with almost no data about the fish in front of them, and much of the most important work is still done by hand, one fish at a time.

We put cameras where fish are already handled, turn every image into measurements, and give farms and plants the tools to act on them. Today that is two products: Phenotyping, which measures every fish for shape, size and condition and links it to its family for breeding decisions, and Digital Twin, which places cameras on processing lines and farm sites onto the floor plan with live views, automatic counts and a built-in AI assistant.

The same per-fish measurements are the foundation for Plant Robotics: robot cells that handle whole fish on the processing line, working alongside the people there. Fish are wet, slippery, soft and never the same twice, which is exactly why this work is still manual and why it needs measurement-driven robots built for food plants rather than rigid grippers and tabletop demos. We are now selecting processing plants for the first pilots on real lines.

We signed a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, and every deployment adds labeled images to a proprietary multi-species dataset that improves our models across species and becomes the brain for autonomous seafood production.

one_liner.before: CV and robotics to automate quality inspection in fish farms
one_liner.after: Building the robotics layer for seafood production
